column8: Thu 19 Nov: store only; the three certainties are background, and the only usable part of Knight (the own-use test) is row 2's.

Thu 19 Nov: 3d wording guard: a holder free to use property for itself holds nothing for anyone else, so her Treasuries are hers, not the residency's or co-sponsors' (with Q3b-033); never held for the residency, set aside for co-sponsors or secured.

Thu 19 Nov: 2.0 contrast half of Goldcorp (quotes checked at source today: certificate of ownership, monthly Peat Marwick audit, registered holder); used only beside row 9, since the Walker and Hall winners held the same certificates.
Thu 19 Nov: store; drop the 2028 deposit from the mapping (her own money to come, no seller's promise); its reasoning is the identified test the card kills for Laura, so never quoted as her rule.
Thu 19 Nov: same test as row 25 and row 2 (a stock its holder may deal in holds nothing for you); Pearson is the closer, commercial twin.

Thu 19 Nov: 2.0 or 3e aha store; quote checked at source, but the card's best five says twenty years later, which is false: Revised Article 8 was approved in 1994, the year of Goldcorp, in another country's law; say the same year, never later.
Thu 19 Nov: printed promises of title give no title is row 3's point; the estoppel detail stays in the card.
Thu 19 Nov: store only; reliance on a promise to keep a separate stock did not move the line; no part needs it.

Thu 19 Nov: 2.0 behind the word owned and 3e's custody line: checked at source today (stored en masse but kept separate, precisely equal, as custodian, same certificates; Board restored Thorp J's remedies); pooled but held apart is owned, Laura's position by statute; never say the Board decided liability afresh.

Thu 19 Nov: 3e's custody line: owning a pool is only as good as the duty to keep it full (lowest balance checked at source), so the watch is the broker's duty, not a vault; custody is one line of 3e prose, never a Table 3 row (SKELETON 4(c), Q72-013).
Thu 19 Nov: store; enough is not owned, a real sufficient stock still gave nothing; Oliver J unread, so cite through Hunter v Moss or Harvard only.
Thu 19 Nov: held apart for named buyers is owned is Walker and Hall's point, which row 9 carries at source; Stapylton Fletcher unread.
Thu 19 Nov: store; the vivid 99 bottles fact for how thin the old goods line was; author unverified in the pages read, so cite the Hamlyn lecture by series and year only; goods law, not securities.
Thu 19 Nov: the same harm (a prepaying buyer from a bulk owned nothing) as row 13, told less plainly.
Thu 19 Nov: store; statute moved the goods line to an undivided share with pro rata loss sharing, the same shape as UCC 8-503(b); no part needs it.
Thu 19 Nov: the US goods version of row 15's point; one statute is enough for the store.
Thu 19 Nov: store; a trust of identical shares without picking which, textbook trust law and contested (row 19), so never the authority for her ownership.
Thu 19 Nov: store; the subject is the pool of one issue, which matches the UCC's per-issue interest (one CUSIP each).
Thu 19 Nov: store guard: Hunter v Moss is doubted, so her ownership rests on the US statute (8-503), never on English case law.
Thu 19 Nov: store; co-ownership of a named pool is the legal shape of held for her in English law.
Thu 19 Nov: a citation detail of Hunter v Moss; the HK and NSW judgments unread.

Thu 19 Nov: store; owned or owed turned on which law applied; UCC 8-110 (which state's law governs her account) unread, and the Australian point is for shares sold before 14 Jul 1986, never Australian law today.
Thu 19 Nov: in her name means registered to her; row 36 carries the same guard in US statute with the stronger-status reason.
Thu 19 Nov: store; its own critique holds: what makes her bonds hers is the credit and the duty to hold (8-501, 8-503, 8-504), not whether the broker traded as agent.

Thu 19 Nov: 3e custody line: a pool its holder may use for itself holds nothing for you; her fully paid holdings may not be used by her broker (Q72-011, whose adapt applies: say the plan buys only with her deposits).
Thu 19 Nov: ownership of a pool presupposes a duty to keep it full is row 10's point; UNIDROIT unread.

Thu 19 Nov: 2.5 guard: a trade binds at the click and title passes at settlement, so never owned the moment she clicked; English law, the US basis is 8-501(b)(1) and T+1 (Q16-013); the 7 Oct click was a WInS order, so no settlement claim is made of it.
Thu 19 Nov: 8-501(b)(1) is store Q72-007, already merged into Q72-008; its 3d use lives in row 43.
Thu 19 Nov: T+1 since 28 May 2024 is in Q16-013; its use line wrongly times ownership after the 7 Oct WInS click, a simulated order with no settlement in law; the guard is row 27's.

Thu 19 Nov: 2.0 wording guard, comment 1 checked at source today: brokers do not segregate so no bond is identified as hers, yet all units are held for customers; kills identified, keeps owned (twin reason to row 32).
Thu 19 Nov: store; comment 1's held in common, timing irrelevant and pro rata (checked at source); the Goldcorp contrast is row 6's.

Thu 19 Nov: 2.0 aha and guard, Official Comment 2 checked at source (not 8-503(b) itself): an entitlement is not a claim to a specific identifiable thing, so owned never means her own bonds; never identified, registered owner or legal owner.
Thu 19 Nov: store; the price of the pool model is a claim against her own broker only; custody is one line of 3e prose, not a Table 3 watch (SKELETON 4(c), Q72-013).
Thu 19 Nov: 2.0, the drafters' own word: a property interest, not a contract claim, coined for this new form of ownership; backs CONCEIT V2.1's owned with Q72-008, one clause at most.
Thu 19 Nov: store; the IPS never says it borrows nothing (Q72-011): say the plan buys only with her deposits; custody is 3e prose, not a Table 3 row, so drop that line.

Thu 19 Nov: wording rule for 2.0, 3b, 3d, 3e: SIPA's customer name securities (78lll(3)-(4) checked at source) make in her name a separate, stronger status she does not have; held for her stays, and Q77-003 must change.
Thu 19 Nov: store, 3e's limit: in a failure SIPA shares all customer property by dollar value, not issue by issue, and the trustee buys back; adds to Q72-012, the record is delay, not loss (8t).
Thu 19 Nov: store; stronger than Q65-027 (press summary read at source), but client money is cash not securities, the dollar figure is a law firm's, and custody is 3e prose, not a Table 3 row.

Thu 19 Nov: 2.0 fact behind owned for a judge who knows gold: a pooled unallocated holder is an unsecured creditor; her Treasuries are pooled like unallocated gold yet owned by statute, the aha; never call any of her holdings allocated.
Thu 19 Nov: owed to you by us against ownership is row 39's line in a bank's model form (read in an excerpt); one bullion fact is enough.
Thu 19 Nov: store guard: never legal owner or registered owner; English law and a third-party copy, so US statute (rows 32, 34) carries the point.

Thu 19 Nov: 2.0 and 3c guard, right on its core (the law draws only ink's word owned; VT is owned yet pencil): drop the 2028 deposit from pencil in both, since in law it may be her own cash or a bank deposit, not a promise.

Thu 19 Nov: 3d, behind SKELETON's custodian statement offered on request (Q22-017): what she can show is the credit, not an audit of enough; Laura's choice, never secured, and her statement also shows VT, which she does not state.

Thu 19 Nov: 2.0 candidate turn, fresh and true at core but the entry is ink is false for her VT entry (owned, still pencil): say the Treasury entries; a certificate is a document, not a figure, and Walker and Hall held the same paper, so the point is the stock held apart; cold test with the definition first.
